title: Sh-L-M
hook: shalom, shalem (whole), shilem (paid): peace means wholeness

segments.voice: Yesterday, shoresh, the three letters under a family of words. Your line: three-letter roots. Today, the first root, under a word you already read.

A receipt stamped paid. A coffee mug with no chips in it. A man limping home after a long, hard night, finally arriving in one piece. And a greeting used coming in and going out. In English they have nothing in common. In Hebrew, the same three letters: shin, lamed, mem. A few days ago you read shalom letter by letter and stopped there. Today we lift out the root, and it turns out to be bigger than the word you thought you knew.
screen: `A RECEIPT STAMPED PAID.` → `A MUG WITH NO CHIPS.` → `HOME IN ONE PIECE.` → `ONE ROOT: SH-L-M.`

segments.voice: Sh-L-M. Four ways in. First, shalem: whole, complete, nothing missing. In Deuteronomy, a merchant is told to keep a weight that is shelemah, whole, and tzedek, just: no shaving a little off when the customer isn't looking. A whole weight is an honest one. Second, shilem: to pay, to make good. In the laws of Exodus, when someone damages what belongs to a neighbor, the Hebrew says he must make it whole, with a verb from this root: restitution, paying it back until nothing is missing. Third, the man limping home. In Genesis, after Jacob wrestles all night and leaves limping, after he meets the brother he feared, the text says he arrived shalem at the city of Shechem. The commentator Rashi reads it three ways: whole in his body, healed; whole in his possessions, even after the gifts he gave away; whole in his learning, having forgotten nothing in his long years away. Fourth, shalom. Read through its root, peace isn't only the absence of a fight. It's wholeness: nothing owed, nothing broken, nothing missing. A home at peace is a home where things are whole between people. When people greet each other with shalom, they may be wishing far more than quiet. Paying what you owe is one way of making something whole.
screen: `SHALEM: A WHOLE, HONEST WEIGHT.` · `SHILEM: PAY IT BACK, MAKE IT WHOLE.` · `JACOB ARRIVES SHALEM.` · `SHALOM: NOTHING OWED, NOTHING MISSING.` · then, large: `PEACE IS WHOLENESS.`

segments.voice: Let your mind look for one small thing still open: a text you owe a reply, a little money borrowed from a friend, a book never returned, a thank you you meant to say. Hold it and notice how it sits, slightly unfinished, then breathe in and feel what whole might be like. If you pray, you can hold that one thing in your prayer.
Sh-L-M. Shin, lamed, mem: the root of shalom, peace; shalem, whole; and shilem, paid. Today's word.
Your line: peace is wholeness. Paying back can be a kind of peace. Day one thousand three hundred fifty-seven.

howItsDone: Jewish teaching connects shalom, peace, with shalem, whole, and the laws of the Torah require paying back what was damaged or borrowed; shalom is also the everyday greeting and a word that closes many prayers.

chat.says: Shalom means peace, right? Like, no fighting?
options: Yes, and more: its root means whole, so peace is nothing owed, broken or missing.
Not quite; shalom only means quiet, like a room where nobody is talking.
Yes, exactly that: shalom just means a war has ended, nothing more to it.
chat.meaning: Shalom shares the root sh-l-m with shalem, whole, and shilem, paid: peace as wholeness, not only the absence of a fight.
